shared.intro: X-ray table models describing the reprocessing of radiation in the circumnuclear environment of accreting supermassive black holes, computed with the ray-tracing radiative-transfer code RefleX 3.0. Each table is a standard XSPEC table model.

tool.name: Line-of-sight NH calculator
tool.description: A command-line utility for computing the line-of-sight column density NH_los for the RXToPo and RXagn1 models using RefleX v3. It provides a simple front-end to the REFLEXINO procedure described in Appendix B of Dimopoulos, Ricci & Paltani (2025), hiding the internal complexity of RefleX and enabling quick calculations for individual sources or batch runs.

references.text: Paltani & Ricci, A&A 607, A31 (2017) — the RefleX code

models.name: RXTorusHR
models.tagline: A dusty torus, computed on a dense parameter grid with a free high-energy cutoff.
models.summary: A dusty torus over 360,000 spectra per component, with the cutoff energy left free.
models.note: RXTorusHR is computed over a wider parameter space than RXToPo: the high-energy cutoff is a free parameter, the photon index spans 1.2 to 3.0, and the covering factor is sampled logarithmically from 0.01 to 0.999.

figure.alt: Schematic of the RXTorusHR geometry: a central black hole with a spherical corona above and below the disk plane, surrounded by a dusty torus of tube radius r at distance R, with the inner edge at the sublimation radius and the viewing angle θ marked.
figure.caption: Geometry of the RXTorusHR model: a dusty torus, with the covering factor set by TorusCF = r / R. Schematic drawn from the model configuration.

overview.value: A dusty torus surrounding the central X-ray source
Cutoff power-law, with both the photon index and the cutoff energy free
20 eV below 10 keV, with 4 eV retained across the Fe Kα, Fe Kβ and Ni Kα windows; 0.01 dex logarithmic binning from 10 to 300 keV
Lodders et al. (2009) abundances, solar metallicity, dust included, H₂ fraction 0.3
Rayleigh scattering, Compton scattering on bound electrons, dust grain interactions
8,000 RefleX runs of 2 × 10⁹ photons each, sampled in 45 inclination bins — 360,000 spectra per component

parameters.name: Ecut
parameters.description: High-energy cutoff of the input continuum; 5 logarithmically spaced values (50, 81.3, 132.3, 215.2, 350 keV), logarithmic interpolation

parameters.name: Pho_index
parameters.description: Photon index Γ of the input cutoff power-law continuum; 10 values in steps of 0.2

parameters.name: TorusNH
parameters.description: Equatorial hydrogen column density of the torus; 16 values, in steps of 0.3 dex up to 23.2 and 0.2 dex from 23.5 upwards

parameters.name: TorusCF
parameters.description: Covering factor of the torus, TorusCF = r / R; 10 logarithmically spaced values, logarithmic interpolation

parameters.name: Obs_angle
parameters.description: Viewing angle θ of the system (1 = face-on, 89 = edge-on); 45 bin centres, every 2°

parameters.name: norm
parameters.description: Photon flux of the input continuum at 1 keV (ph keV⁻¹ cm⁻² s⁻¹)

notes.title: Note on the normalisation.
notes.text: The simulations were run at a fixed 2 – 10 keV luminosity, identical for every (Pho_index, Ecut) pair. The tabulated fluxes have been corrected to the standard XSPEC cutoffpl photon normalisation — A = 1 ph keV⁻¹ cm⁻² s⁻¹ at 1 keV — so the table norm can be tied directly to the norm of a cutoffpl component with the same Pho_index and Ecut.

notes.title: Note on the covering factor and the torus size.
notes.text: The sublimation radius is held fixed at r_sub = 3.107 × 10¹⁷ cm. The torus tube radius follows from the covering factor as r = TorusCF / (1 − TorusCF) × r_sub, and its distance from the black hole is R = r_sub + r, so that TorusCF = r / R. The volume density of the material is set by the equatorial column density as n = NH / 2r.

notes.title: Note on the X-ray source.
notes.text: The continuum is emitted by two spherical sources placed symmetrically above and below the disk plane, at 10 gravitational radii with a radius of 6 gravitational radii, for a black hole mass of 10^6.23 solar masses.

dataset.citation: Dimopoulos, G. (2026). RXTorusHR: high-resolution X-ray table models for a dusty torus (Version v1) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22699166

models.name: RXToPo
models.tagline: Reprocessed emission from a dusty torus with a polar hollow cone.
models.summary: A dusty torus plus a polar hollow cone — the baseline geometry for obscured AGN.

figure.alt: Schematic of the RXToPo geometry: a central black hole and corona, a dusty torus of inner radius r and outer radius R, and a polar hollow cone, with the inclination angle θ, the torus half-opening angle φ and the cone outer boundary ξ_o marked.
figure.caption: Geometry of the RXToPo model. Figure from Dimopoulos, Ricci & Paltani (2025), ApJ 992, 64.

notes.title: Note on the polar cone opening angle.
notes.text: The hollow cone is collimated by the torus. Its inner boundary angle is set to ξ_max = φ + 1° (to avoid overlap), where φ = arcsin(CFtor). The cone has a fixed angular width of 10°, so its outer boundary is ξ_o = ξ_max + 10°. The cone column density NHpol is a free parameter independent of CFtor.

notes.title: Note on the total sky coverage.
notes.text: The total covering fraction of obscuring material is not equal to CFtor alone. The polar cone also contributes solid angle coverage and should be accounted for when computing the total covering factor.

models.provenance: Developed at the Instituto de Estudios Astrofísicos, Universidad Diego Portales, Santiago, Chile, with the support of ANID Beca Doctorado Nacional 21211606.

models.name: RXagn1
models.tagline: Full circumnuclear AGN model including a dusty torus, polar hollow cone, accretion disk, and broad line region.
models.summary: Everything in RXToPo, plus the accretion disk and broad line region.
models.note: RXagn1 differs from RXToPo only in geometry. All other technical details — continuum, energy range, resolution, composition and parameters — are identical.

figure.alt: Schematic of the RXagn1 geometry: as RXToPo, with a central black hole, corona, dusty torus and polar hollow cone, and in addition an accretion disk (AD) and a broad line region (BLR) close to the black hole.
figure.caption: Geometry of the RXagn1 model, adding the accretion disk and broad line region. Figure from Dimopoulos, Ricci & Paltani (2025), ApJ 992, 64.

notes.title: Note on the polar cone opening angle.
notes.text: The hollow cone is collimated by the torus. Its inner boundary angle is set to ξ_max = φ + 1° (to avoid overlap), where φ = arcsin(CFtor). The cone has a fixed angular width of 10°, so its outer boundary is ξ_o = ξ_max + 10°. The cone column density NHpol is a free parameter independent of CFtor.

notes.title: Note on the total sky coverage.
notes.text: The total covering fraction of obscuring material is not equal to CFtor alone. The polar cone also contributes solid angle coverage and should be accounted for when computing the total covering factor.
